I find myself getting dehydrated a lot, but when I tell myself I have to drink 3 of these it makes it much easier! I also love how the button pops the lid right open.

The only thing I dislike about this bottle is that the lid breaks too easily! I got my first water bottle and accidentally dropped it onto the floor when I was at work. A crack formed right next to the button, making it impossible to close. So, I decided to get a second one because I loved my first one so much. I had the second for about 2 months, before I once again accidentally dropped it and again had almost the same exact crack next to the button, again making it impossible to close.

Bottom line, it's a great water bottle, just DO NOT DROP IT!!!! BE CAREFUL NOT TO DROP IT!!!!

text_fidelity_a:
Electric Foot Warmer for Men and Women with Non-Slip，Fast Heating Pad with Four Layer Temperature Locking System,Foot Warmer Under Desk.Electric Foot Heating pad with 3 Temperature Settings. The foot warmer seems to be made of good quality fabric and leather.

The foot warmer has three temperature settings: 38C (100F), 42C (108F), and 55C (131F). When I turned the foot warmer on at room temperature, it listed 22C. I adjusted the temperature to the hottest setting of 55C. I kept it going for 45 minutes, with both my feet in the warmer. After 20 minutes or so the warmer stabilized at a temperature of 43 to 44C. 25 minutes later, the temperature had not changed, never reaching anywhere close to 55C. 44C was warm enough, but not what was promised.

Besides the temperature limit, two drawbacks for me (may not apply to other people):
- The foot warmer has USB-C input, and it comes with a USB-A to USB-C cable. Note that the warmer only accepts 10W, and if you try to use a USB-C to USB-C cable that delivers higher wattage, the foot warmer will not work. Ideally the foot warmer's electronics would be designed to take as much wattage as they need, and no more, in the same way I can connect an iphone and an ipad pro to the same fast-charging brick, and each device would accept only as much wattage as appropriate, instead of burning out or shutting down.
- This foot warmer seems to be designed for those who shoe sizes 11 and under. I wear size 13 shoes, and my feet barely fit, with my toes partially curled. Pretty uncomfortable. The product description makes no reference to foot size, and unfortunately for me, I cannot use this foot warmer effectively. Otherwise, it does its job well.
text_fidelity_b: Electric Foot Warmer for Men and Women with Non-Slip，Fast Heating Pad with Four Layer Temperature Locking System,Foot Warmer Under Desk.Electric Foot Heating pad with 3 Temperature Settings.

Smart Weighted Hula Hoops for Adults Weight Loss Non-Fall Exercise Hoola Hoop Detachable Adjustable Size Abdomen Fitness Massage Professional Intelligent Counter Workout for Women Men and Kids Blue I looked at tons of weighted hoola hoops on Amazon and saw many of them has some not so great reviews because they were no sturdy or would break apart. This hoola hoop is definitely very sturdy and well made.

It comes in several pieces that link together so you can adjust it to fit your waist and ideally remove pieces as you lose weight. The pieces link together very well, it feels very secure. The weight is also very secure in the hoola hoop.

I find it to be a really fun way to work out. You do feel the burn with this especially if you do the full recommended 30 mins. It took me 2 days to get the hang of it, I watched a couple youtube videos for some tips. Basically, you want to shift your weight side to side rather than do a full circular motion with your hips.

I have been using it for about 2 weeks now - about every other day and I noticed a slight decrease in my waist but nothing crazy yet, though I do believe doing this for a month at least 5 days a week will give you noticeable results.

Currently, I am able to go for about 10 mins straight without stopping at all. Whenever I stop, I switch directions. The only downside that I have noticed is when I use it in the opposite direction, the counter on the hoop doesn't count those spins. It only counts going in one direction. I don't know if that's just something wrong with my counter or if that's how it's made but ultimately it's not that big of an issue (though it would be nice to have an accurate count of my total spins at the end of the workout).

Also, it is loud like others have mentioned - but I think all of these kind of hoola hoops are. If you wear headphones you can easily listen to a podcast or watch youtube or something - but you can't really without headphones.

Overall, if you're looking for a weighted hoola hoop, this one is a good one!
text_fidelity_b: Smart Weighted Hula Hoops for Adults Weight Loss Non-Fall Exercise Hoola Hoop Detachable Adjustable Size Abdomen Fitness Massage Professional Intelligent Counter Workout for Women Men and Kids Blue

Imagine my disappointment when the first whistle that I tried wasn't that loud. It just gave a muffled sort of whistle. It would probably be loud enough if I blew as hard as I could, though. The whistle is 2 3/16" long and 5/8" wide and 3/8" deep, so they don't take up that much room. They are lightweight. The lanyard is about 16 inches long when major doubled, lying flat (from the back of the neck to the whistle rather than the length from the whistle all the way around that point again).

text_fidelity_a:
Weaver Leather Throw Line Storage Bag Are you a ham radio operator tossing portable antennas up into trees? Don't like the idea of sling shots and potato launchers? Hate that tangled mess of mason line? Looking for reasonable elevation for the weekend? I recommend this.

I hate rope, string, wine, wire, cable, and anything squiggly that is over 25 feet long. It is certain to become a tangled mess and cost 30 minutes to an hour to straighten out just to have it wrap around your ankle and trip you up. Happens to me every single time.

Some smart ham out there suggested I try this throw line bag and weight. After it was delivered I brought it out to the backyard and started tossing it around. I made about five or six long low tosses without any tangles and three or four high tosses over the tree without a problem. I'm sold on it. My slingshot is going to see a lot less use and I still don't have the guts to try my potato launcher.

The bag is more than storage. After a toss you just stuff the line back in the bag without concern for winding it properly. Just push it down in the bag. When tossing the weight you just let the line play out of the bag. I have yet to experience a tangle. I'm sure there's some added resistance and I might be losing a foot or two of max height but for ease of storage and deployment you can have the foot.

When done, stuff the line in the bag along with the weight. Cinch it up and toss back in the truck until next time. Not a whole lot of fussing.

A warning... wear gloves. The rope they use burns! Me and one other person found out the hard way. Ya... I didn't tell him. But even after that he went out and bought his own kit so maybe the burn wasn't so bad. Still, wear gloves.

I think I got the 12 oz weight. Then next one down might have been a little better. After a few tosses of the 12 oz weight I was getting real tired and my height/distance was dropping rapidly. Good argument for doing it right the first time I guess. Still, 8 oz might be some benefit.

I know it's tempting but don't toss this thing at your buddies. The weight is substantial and if you hit them they won't share in your amusement. Not that I did anything like that but you know. It could happen.

That's it. Wish I found this a long time ago. Until now I had been using my slingshot with a 1 oz weight and a Zebco 33 and 20 lb test line. Then I would tie the mason line for the second pass. The tangles were unbelievable so a spool of mason line was a one-time-use item for me. The rope in this kit is strong enough to hold up any wire antenna for a weekend so you only need a single pass.
text_fidelity_b: Weaver Leather Throw Line Storage Bag

text_fidelity_a:
Nike Golf Xtreme Sport IV Golf Bag First, to establish my street cred, I'm retired and play lots of golf. Last year I played 118 rounds. I play year around and walk/carry, walk with push cart, and ride in a cart, mostly depending on weather. I need a bag that is easy to carry but also also works on carts. I like to have all my stuff with me in my bag. Rain gear, extra gloves, rangefinder, umbrella, sunscreen, water bottle, Advil, windbreaker, cigars, towels, balls, tees, etc. you get the picture.

This bag is nice looking, but after playing a few rounds with it, it seems it was designed by a designer, not a golfer. It's attractive and generally speaking, it's functional. But there are a few things I can mention that are why I'm deducting a couple stars. Golfers like me will know what I'm talking about.

The good things: I like the dividers. There are several and they keep the clubs well-separated so you can easily see each iron and don't have to shuffle the heads around to find your 9-iron. The legs pop out solidly and pop back in crisply when you pick it up. It is very, very light....so all the weight you will feel is from the stuff you load into it. The carrying straps are wide and comfortable and there is some nice padding on the side that hits your back. The insulated cooler pocket is nice, but I haven't had a chance yet to see how it does in 100 degree Texas heat. Gotta be better than nothing though right?

The issues: While not necessarily show-stoppers, these things could be better. When you load this bag onto an electric golf cart, the golf cart strap you pull around your bag to hold it on comes right across the top of two zippered pockets. In other words, if you want to get into those two pockets on your bag, you have to either a) unhook the strap holding your bag on, or b) keep those zippers halfway down to be able to get into them.

The next thing is also somewhat minor, but worth mentioning. I have a Sun Mountain Speed Cart, which is a 3-wheeled push cart you set your carry bag on when you don't to carry it. This bag is a little bigger than my old Titleist carry bag, and it doesn't "nest" into the arms of the push cart perfectly. It works, but this bag kind of sits a little awkwardly in the Speed Cart.

The zippers. The reason I needed a new bag was that the nylon zippers on my old bag finally failed. You know how nylon zippers will ultimately just not zip? The zipper thing goes up and down, but the two sides stay apart. Well anyway, this bag has nylon zippers too of course, and these seem to be of lighter duty than my old bag. They may end up working fine for years....but they are definitely of a smaller and more dainty construction.

Finally...the thing I am most disappointed in is the zippered pockets themselves. Remember I said this was created by a designer rather than a golfer? Well, when you unzip the pockets, you can slide your open hand in and feel both sides of the pocket pressing on your hand! It's like they are designed for small flat stuff! The big front pocket for golf balls is the only one with ample room. The others are very tight and I'm worried cramming all my stuff in there is going to put too much pressure on those dainty zippers!

The price is attractive, and hopefully it will hold up to the beating I am about to give it. If somebody reminds me in a few months, I'll update my review after putting it through the paces of several dozen rounds. Fore!
text_fidelity_b: Nike Golf Xtreme Sport IV Golf Bag

PROs

All in all I love this bag and would definitely recommend it.

text_fidelity_a:
SEAFLO 42-Series Water Pressure Diaphragm Pump w/Variable Flow For Reduced Cycling - 12V, 3.0GPM, 55PSI This is an interesting pump. It works really well, but there are some things to keep in mind.

First, it's a 1/2" line. In and out. Hooking it up to a 5/8" or 3/4" hose really cuts the pressure. However, put it on a 1/2" line (I used PEX) and the pressure is good.

Second, the NPT connections work really well, but you will need some adapters if you want to connect it to other things. There is a Garden hose threat adapter out there for a fair price. However, the barbed connector provided doesn't work well with PEX. There are PEX to NPT connectors easily available.

Third, you need a good, ridged intake pipe. I tried some clear poly tubing and it more or less collapsed as the intake. Of course that really cut down on the output.

So, with the correct adapters you can get it to work well for things other than campers. Just don't expect it to be "plug and play".
text_fidelity_b: SEAFLO 42-Series Water Pressure Diaphragm Pump w/Variable Flow For Reduced Cycling - 12V, 3.0GPM, 55PSI

text_fidelity_a:
KEEPTO Exercise Resistance Band Set with Handles,5 Fitness Workout Bands for Women at Home Gym We have a large array of options for working out - to loose/keep off weight and build and maintain muscle. But among the options we wanted something that we could travel with as well as give us a variety of options at home. Boredom can kill a workout routine.

I specifically chose this set for 1. the variety and choices of weights, 2. The options for use with/without a door, 3. The look of the hand and ankle straps and handles, 4. The look of the ends of the bands - their connector including the carabiner connectors.

1. The variety of weights/resistance allows one to go up to 120 lbs. We are not there, but we have the option. Changing the bands out can give a range of weight options and this was a good one compared to others. It also lets one adjust what they are doing - legs, arms.

2. The options for use with or without a door means one can anchor the bands under one’s foot or in a door. We have a TRX set we use with a door, but this gives us another option - we would be more likely to travel with this set now so if unable to use in a door on a trip we would still have the ability to use our feet. That said, there is something “better” to a TRX version. It feels stronger - but it is slightly heavier, while this set is more complicated with all the items included.

3. The hand and ankle straps appeared average overall, but better than some other sets we were looking at. The handles are a bit “rough,” but not uncomfortable. I have worked them with and without gloves and both are fine. The ankle straps are average in feel, but better than some I’ve experienced. Overall both are just fine.

4. I was mostly concerned that they would have longevity. I looked at how the bands connected to the handles, how they were topped off to keep their own ends secure. Compared to others - via pictures - these appeared to have good, solid endings, and that the make up of how they connect to the handles was a good method. I know the carabiners are the weakest link and I took that into consideration. I think they are pretty solid - based on pictures and how they feel - but I am prepared should they fail - we would be able to change them out for others if needed.

Overall we are happy with this choice. The set is what it appears to be, but compared to many others - and I looked at more than 20 sets - this one had everything we wanted, feels as though it has the longevity and strength we wanted and expect, and will give us another successful workout option.

Happy to recommend.
text_fidelity_b: KEEPTO Exercise Resistance Band Set with Handles,5 Fitness Workout Bands for Women at Home Gym

text_fidelity_a: Edge 61135-7 H20 Quiver Magnet These little decoy aids are great, but you have to do a couple of things before you use them, or you will experience the problems others noted. 1. spray the switch, motor and battery contacts with a good Teflon oil. 2. get a package of Remington Camo wrap and cut to fit the top of the cover 3. be sure to tighten the lid securely.  I hunt a very natural blind with about 2 dozen decoys positioned in sets of six and I add three of these aids to each set. For storage and ease of setup, I keep them on slip rigs in sets of three separated with a D ring for each three.  As another hunter noted, they are not intended to move your decoys, but to add some motion to the water within your decoy set.  I can tell you they do make a big difference in bringing in the ducks, especially on still days.  When needed, take the time to replace the batteries at the end of the days hunt and you'll be ready for the next hunt.  One final tip, don't forget that mallards and other puddle ducks only feed in water 12" to 15" deep or less, and these aids mimic a feeding duck.
text_fidelity_b: Edge 61135-7 H20 Quiver Magnet

Additional features I didn't use:

I didn't find the belt to be comfortable in that position--my legs hit the bottles when running. Instead, I've worn it with the pocket and bottles on my back, and then I barely notice I am wearing the belt with its bottles.

text_fidelity_a:
Henderson Women's Thermoprene 3mm Front Zip Shorty Springsuit, Black/Lavender, 8 I got my first Henderson Zip Shorty a couple years ago for snorkelling on the Big Island. It was SUPERB! There is simply no easier style for getting into and out of a wetsuit on hot, steamy days or peeling them off when they're all wet. It's super easy to step into one of the legs and then zip the shorty up as high as you like. There is JUST the right amount of give in the armpits so you can swim but not fill the suit with water. It's a brilliant design, actually. The 3mm thickness was absolutely perfect for swimming in HI's water - where temps averaged 71-74F for us.

After each use, I'd faithfully soak, then rinse the suit out with special neoprene detergent, then roll it in a beach towel and hang it up to dry in the shower stall. It would be clean, fresh, dry and ready to use within a couple hours - even in a humid place.

I wore a long-sleeved rashguard under mine for extra sun protection, but otherwise, was totally warm enough with great flexibility for swimming in this garment. At the end of our 3-mo stay in HI, I donated my Henderson - and the dive shop nearly cried for joy!

Flash forward 2 years, and I bought the identical suit for snorkelling on Kauai! If I was psychic, I never would've donated the last one, and now I'm going to be an optimist and keep this one!

CAVEAT!!! Be sure to soak, WASH, rinse your suit out before you try it on - seriously! I just wore mine for 10-15 min day one and woke up later that night with a shorty-shaped RASH on my skin. I only read about neoprene reactions after that - and immediately washed my new shorty. Err on the cautious side, cuz that was the one and only time I got a rash, and you can avoid that if you just wash it first.

Of course, if you don't want to remove the tags, you could also try your wetsuit on with a "skin" underneath - but be sure to wash that garment then to avoid any neoprene reaction.
text_fidelity_b: Henderson Women's Thermoprene 3mm Front Zip Shorty Springsuit, Black/Lavender, 8

This was a frustrating, but easy set to put together.
First, the pieces are few: the two U bars, 4 bases, screws with washers, little wrench, and 2 hand grips. The hand grips are on, but are velcro so they can be removed and returned.

The set is easy to put together, one person can really do it in about 10 minutes.

That said, it was a but frustrating: having to hold the screw in place while turning the wrench - the little wrench kept sliding off the screw head and there is nothing to hold the other side - other than your hand - to help tighten. It worked, but it took awhile, and it was frustrating. Perhaps using another wrench of your own, but 1. they emphasis not over tightening and use of another tool might encourage that, and 2. I didn’t feel like I needed it in the end. Yes, a little rough, but it worked as is. I would strongly encourage checking tightness from time to time.

I’ve used it a few times and find my weight doesn’t let me do it too much yet, but I’m able to maintain what I do on the ground. I plan to use this intermittently with the ground and another piece of equipment I have. My wife too has used it and with less weight to lift is already able to do both push ups and reverse push ups. It’s a great height, the weight keep it secure - we have used it on living room carpet - and is not at all too heavy to move around. It is a large set, meaning you’ll have to find somewhere to keep it. But it’s not so large as to not be usable.

Overall this is a great set and we are happy to have added it to our workout equipment. This will get great usage and is already contributing to our love of competition. Happy to recommend.

JAPER BEES Bocce Ball Set Solid Resin 90mm Outdoor Lawn Games for Family with 8 Balls 1 Pallino Measuring Rope Canvas Carrying Case If I could give this JAPER BEES Bocce Ball Set a 10 star rating I would! My wife and I are thrilled to have it! A few months ago my wife several broke her foot and has been off it. As the doctor lets her get back on it - and encourages slow exercise to help her rebuild leg muscles, I wanted to find something for her to do that would get her up, but not over do it. Bocce Ball can be played over a very large area - we controlled it by just going back and forth - but it got us outside, into the sun, and moving. She could take breaks and we had a blast! I grabbed the regulation set - figuring it was best overall for weight and size. I have never played before and she hadn’t played since she was a teen. We had to use the instructions, but it was pretty easy to learn. And our local park was the perfect place.

1. It comes in a great bag - the full set fits well into the bag, which is well designed and built. It’s a strong material, looks great - with the logo - and the zipper is strong. This is a pretty heavy set of balls and this bag holds up well. It looks great out there too.
2. There are three nets in the bag, each holding 3 balls - or two balls and the small ball and measuring string.
3. There is a set of instructions - my wife read it and talked me through it. It’s been easy to learn and play.
4. The balls for this set weigh a great amount - it wasn’t long before we had a feel for them and able to play well - a difference between long play or short.
5. The balls can take it. In this state the ground is a bit hard and the grass isn’t the best, and we were throwing them a good distance. After 3 games over 2 days they still look perfect. I’m not saying we beat them up, but we put them through playing - these are really nice. They look nice, hold nice, have a great balance. I really have no game of reference, but this is a great set.

I literally played for the first time this weekend and I loved it! This was a great game for my wife and I - not just as she recovers from her foot injury, but in general. We have every intention of getting many years out of this set - playing often. We took it easy because of her recovery, but we know we’ll be able to cover a lot of ground in the future (grass, sand, whatever). It is a fun game with a need for some talent - but yet something most nay member of the family can play. Our regulation set is fairly heavy - we are guessing not as heavy as tournament - so something to consider if playing with kids. But we have had a lot of fun, shared a lot of laughs, and enjoyed spending the time playing. We are thrilled with this JAPER BEES Bocce Ball Set and look forward to many more years playing.

text_fidelity_a:
IRONMAN Triathlon X-Class 310 Smart Technology Upright Bike with Bluetooth Apps, Air Soft Seat and BONUS Equipment Mat I have only had this a few days so will update the review if needed in the future.

Initial impressions have been very positive so far for the build and quality of the bike. I found the instructions very good and easy to follow. They were well written which is amazing all by itself. I had no problems following the instructions and it took about 45 minutes to put together. The only issue I ran into was the handle bar cover (small plastic piece that covers mounting screws), almost got thrown away, as it is in the packing material where everything else was a bit separate. Just make sure you don't accidently throw it away.

The bike seems to be very well built, and parts all lined up without any issues during assembly. A couple of parts are a bit on the heavy side so you might need someone to help you hold the handle bar support bar while you make the electronic connections, other than that I expect most folks should be able to put this together on their own.

Pros:
Once assembled the bike itself is very sturdy and feels very strong. I am a big person 6'8, and it supports me without any issues.
Very quiet, in fact the little fan is louder than peddling the bike. The fan is not load by any measure, but the bike is very quiet.
Great assembly instructions and packaging
Nice mat included

Cons:
Bluetooth integration -- This is very poor unfortunately. While you can sync to the app, you can't sync to your music or audio on your device so the speakers will not work without attaching the included cable to your device.
Andriod app -- This is very poor. Basically it shows you your speed and some of the stats, but you lose all functionality of the built in computer in this mode. this means you have to set the resistance manually and can't use any of the programs or features. The app itself has no built in programs so you have to manually adjust the resistance as you go along. Also doesn't seem to work with any other of the much better rated apps that are available. The current app has a 2 star rating, and I think 2 stars would be stretch for this software.
text_fidelity_b: IRONMAN Triathlon X-Class 310 Smart Technology Upright Bike with Bluetooth Apps, Air Soft Seat and BONUS Equipment Mat

text_fidelity_a:
PackIt Freezable Utility Cooler, 18 Can, Charcoal Grey The main, cooled compartment is 10.5" x 7.5" x 7" tall. It is a family-sized cooler bag for food or beverages. The gel for cooling is in the front, bottom, and back walls of the cooler. The side walls are just canvas and do not contain gel, and I don't think the top has gel either. The cooler walls can be collapsed so the cooler is flatter and smaller when you place it in the freezer. They recommend cooling it in the freezer for 12 hours before use. There is a zippered, flat outside pocket in the front that is 8.5" wide and 5.5" tall. There is a handle on top of the of the cooler under which is a compartment that will hold things like napkins, phones, utensils, etc. The opening is 5.5" wide. There is no zipper to secure this pocket. Due to the handle being right above the opening for this area, it is not highly convenient to get things in and out. This compartment is about 2" deep and covers the entire width and length of the lid. There is also a zippered, flat outer pocket tucked away on the bottom of the bag. It has an attached pull-out bit of fabric, though I'm not sure what it's for. I'm also not sure what you'd want to place in this pocket, since it's between the ground and the bottom gel wall of the cooler and weight will be on it. The cooler also has an adjustable carry strap. The cooler interior is easy to clean up if there are spills. It seems to be working okay to keep food cool for a few hours while traveling.

text_fidelity_a:
Birchwood Casey Shoot-N-C, 8" Targets, Adhesive, See Hits Instantly At the time I bought this 30 pack the price was $20 delivered for a per-target price of $0.66 each. This is a great value, as the local Wal-Mart sells a pack that is about $1 each.

Each target is a peel-and-stick "label". It adheres excellent to cardboard and clean, flat surfaces. I adheres OK to rougher surfaces like old, splintering plywood. I affixed this directly to an old shot-up apple crate and ended up having to supplement a little duct tape to keep it on when the wind kicked up.

Every target has four "pasties" that you can peel off and affix to the target after you've shot it. Each pasty is large enough to cover 2 or 3 .45 caliber holes, depending on how close your grouping is. The pasties are useful enough to extend each target by at least one more shooting group.

Here is a great suggestion to really extend the life of each target -- if you have guns of multiple calibers, start with your lowest caliber and work your way up. You can easily tell the difference between your .22 caliber hitsvs. your 9mm vs. your .45 caliber.

Using this methodology, you could probably use a single target up to 6 times, unless you are a nail driver and shoot out your bullseye really quickly!

The only downsides I can say are:

1) These targets are much more expensive than paper targets, but they're so easy to see that they're totally worth it for practicing your shooting and making adjustments after each shot.

2) The pasties can sometimes fly off when they get hit. Make sure you give them a good press and seal.
text_fidelity_b: Birchwood Casey Shoot-N-C, 8" Targets, Adhesive, See Hits Instantly

text_fidelity_a: GoZafu Outdoor Meditation Cushion Very nice! I’ve been looking for an outdoor-compatible and travel-friendly meditation cushion. This is compact, surprisingly comfortable, and makes it very easy and comfortable to keep your back erect (even easier than my normal buckwheat-hull zafu). I had been looking at it for quite awhile before buying due to its high price, seems like $50-60 would be more in line with my expectations, but it is of high quality, very heavy-duty, and comfortable enough I plan to use it for some at-home sessions as well as parks/hiking/travel (not to mention backyard!). The fold-out skirt is small, but helpful for reducing dirt/gravel annoyances. The design seems like a version 1.5, works well but still a bit rough in spots - at some point they ought to get rid of the not-for-end-user large zipper (or if they keep it, make it usable by the consumer e.g. for laundering the cover). The size and shape of the skirt and seat aren’t 100%, but they are surprisingly good. There are a number of things that could be made a bit lighter, for those planning to go backpacking with it. At some point they may want to consider an “xl” model as well, I am 5’10”, athletic/muscular build, 180#, and though I understand the seat is only intended to support the sit bones, it is very close, and I’m used to having another inch or so of coverage on either side, and the skirt - while helpful - is still small enough that my knees can have ground contact. That said, very well done. Don’t know why noone’s done something like this before.

text_fidelity_a:
Fitbit Charge 4 Special Edition Fitness and Activity Tracker with Built-in GPS, Heart Rate, Sleep & Swim Tracking, Black/Granite Reflective, One Size (S &L Bands Included) I admit up front that I'm not using this to it's full capacity because my interests are more narrow: I don't want to check email or make calls from my activity tracker, I just want it to track my activities. However, more basic trackers proved to be cheap in quality as well as price, so the FitBit charge was a compromise choice for me.

For the things I care most about, it works well in general. It's good for tracking the activities I care about, and it only took it a few weeks to learn to recognize spontaneous activities that I sometimes do without starting the workout timer. It reliably buzzes to remind me to get moving every hour, another key feature that I needed, although I wish it were possible to set a goal of something like 10 hours out of 12 rather than a set number of straight hours. Still, that's a pretty minor complaint.

Sleep tracking seems to work okay, but I don't use it as much as I intended because I find sleeping with the band annoying. It's not uncomfortable; it's just not part of my sleep routine and I gave up on sleep tracking. I suspect that just knowing that I'm wearing it to track my sleep makes me slightly anxious, which in turn makes me less likely to fall asleep. However, for the nights I have worn it, the numbers seem to accord with my subjective experience of the night. One thing about this is that you have to be asleep for three hours before the tracking starts. I'm sure FitBit have good reasons for this, but it would be more useful to me if it started at the two hour mark.

The health metrics are interesting but aren't something I need.

I found the mobile app a little tricky at first but got used to it after several weeks. The website is nice for looking at everything on one big screen, but I don't have much use for it beyond that.

The GPS seems to work very well and consistently.

Battery life isn't great -- I charge mine at least every other day.

The band that came in the box was comfortable and worked well but broke after six months. Luckily, I was able to get a replacement from a third-party seller -- it's bulkier than the original but also more durable.
text_fidelity_b: Fitbit Charge 4 Special Edition Fitness and Activity Tracker with Built-in GPS, Heart Rate, Sleep & Swim Tracking, Black/Granite Reflective, One Size (S &L Bands Included)

text_fidelity_a:
Swagman XC2 Hitch Mount Bike Rack , Black, 2-Inch Receiver Easy to setup and adjust, feels sturdy and secure. It really would take a bit of effort to remove a bike from it if you have it locked down.

Seems like a really good value.

There were a few stumbling blocks I encountered, though. First, the locking hitch pin that Sawgman sells is a bit expensive, compared to other locking pins you can find. However, because the rack had a threaded hole, a standard 1/2” pin won’t fit through. I ended up just yawing the supplied pin, and used a small Master Lock with a small enough shackle diameter to fit. Probably not as secure as the proprietary locking pin, but it should be enough to dissuade anyone looking for a quick grab and go.

Speaking of shackle diameter, it was a bit of a challenge to find the perfect locks to use on the bars. Your typical MasterLock is about 7mm, which is too big; and 5mm was small enough that you could still pull the trigger and move the bar up with ease. In the end I found the MasterLock 141T set of two locks (Keyed alike) with a 6mm shackle was the best fit. The shackle is just small enough to fit through the hole, but thick enough to keep the trigger secure.

So the TLDR, but a lock with a 6mm diameter shackle to secure your bikes.
text_fidelity_b: Swagman XC2 Hitch Mount Bike Rack , Black, 2-Inch Receiver

text_fidelity_a: Rocket stove with handle, A portable wood burning camping stove with a fire poker & tongs. wood burning Rocket stove with Large Fuel Chamber Best for outdoor cooking. tent heater & emergency. I have messed around with DIY rocket stoves with some success - my best was in using concrete blocks.  They work, but who wants to carry around 4 or 6 concrete blocks in their car?  It's not awful, but this rocket stove is lighter weight and works pretty much the same way.  One really good deal with this rocket stove is that it has the slide on grate pieces so that a pot/pan can be put on top to cook food, boil water for coffee or whatever.  It also gives off heat so when you are out camping, you can sit near it while cooking and not worry about the wind changing direction and open flames burning you as might happen with a regular fire.  Not just that, but with this rocket stove, you can gather small twigs that wouldn't keep a regular fire going and in a rocket stove, they burn well.  I think if I were to make any changes to this design, I'd change the legs.  I'm no engineer, but I think a folding mechanism could be used so the legs are permanently attached, but fold down so the rocket stove is as small as it is now (without the legs being removed and possibly lost).  The same with the slide on grate pieces.  Again, I am not an engineer so it may be that hinges that close to heat might be an issue, but if the grate pieces could be slightly curved so they rest against the stove pipe section, then the same would be accomplished with them as the legs.  The less you have to keep track of, the less that can be lost, right?  Of course if you have a "rocket rucksack" to store it in and maybe the inside is that heat mat stuff so you could place it under the stove while using it and then fold it up to store the stove in it...hey, just some suggestions to the manufacturer for the next iteration!  As far as this rocket stove goes, I am very pleased with it's performance.
text_fidelity_b: Rocket stove with handle, A portable wood burning camping stove with a fire poker & tongs. wood burning Rocket stove with Large Fuel Chamber Best for outdoor cooking. tent heater & emergency.

text_fidelity_a:
Dead On Tools DO-300 Killer Chiller Mobile Cooler/Lunch box, Black I bought this for my husband who works outside and needed something to keep lunch plus multiple drinks cold all day.
PROS:
- Very large size - can hold 2 larger-sized gatorade drinks PLUS a 16.9 oz water bottle in the bottom compartment with an ice pack, and 2 sandwiches with 2 16.9 oz water bottles or more on top
- Very sturdy material - thick, tear resistant, very durable
- Comes with optional shoulder strap that fits perfectly in the front zippered compartment if you need to be hands free
- Looks more masculine than LL Bean-type of lunch bags so hubby actually uses it
- Front pocket is see through mesh and perfect to hold strap and a "tick key" tick remover for outdoor use
- At under 20 bucks, it's a real bargain! I bought an extra one and put it away for when this one bites the dust

CONS:
- Black color means it gets hot outdoors or in the car - especially if the sun hits it
- White interior shows every bit of dirt (although cleans up easily with a little baking soda-water paste on a sponge)
- Zippers are sturdy, but get "stuck" quite often
- Sides are soft so will the bag will sit lop-sided if unequal size items are placed in the bottom
- Triangular shaped top (with above mentioned soft sides) makes it so things on top are easily crushed
- Top handles are too small too fit a large sized wrist through so it must be carried by hand or shoulder strap

All in all a good lunch box for men (and women) who carry lots of food and drinks for lunch. I wish there were other color options- maybe an army green or tan- so it didn't get so hot in the sun. Would also be better if at least the bottom compartment had stiff sides. Also, a zippered pouch or compartment to hold a cold pack would be nice, so it didn't have to get mixed in with contents.

It's really hard to find a durable, masculine lunch box for guys who get dirty at work or work outdoors. I've looked for something decent for years and the selection is extremely limited. This fits the bill and is very reasonably priced. For under 20 bucks, you can't do any better than this!
text_fidelity_b: Dead On Tools DO-300 Killer Chiller Mobile Cooler/Lunch box, Black

Gerber Answer FAST Knife, Serrated Edge [22-41970] Well, first off this is my first assisted opening knife, so operationally it was new to me flicking it out. Anyway, about the knife, it is a very well made. I have no problems with the quality of the construction of the knife.

But, how would it work for self defense situations? I carried it this weekend to see how easy it would be to get to it in a quick deployment situation. What I found is that the clip was to tight and it would be difficult to get off of my pocket. ok, no big deal, pair of needle nose pliers and it is looser. But what I noticed beyond that was that the single button used for locking and releasing the blade can cause deployment problems. Wanting to show off my new knife to a buddy of mine, I pulled it out of my pocket and tried to flip the blade. Damn, it was locked, good thing it wasn't a bad guy. What I found is that when you put the blade in your pocket, or when you reach for it, there is a very very good chance you have put the button in the lock position. So when you pull it out to deploy if it is locked, it is locked and you have to unlock it before flicking it out. Unfortunately you cannot disable this feature because this button also serves to lock the blade out and releases the blade for folding. So, unless you can train yourself in a very stressful self def situation to use fine motor skills to unlock a button, I wouldn't use it in that capacity.

So bottom line, good knife, but wouldn't use it for self defense purposes. I'll keep carrying my other non assisted opening Gerber knife for self defense.
text_fidelity_b: Gerber Answer FAST Knife, Serrated Edge [22-41970]

East West U.S.A RTC530 Tactical Molle Attachment Smartphone Phone Holster If you get a good one this is a great phone holder. Unfortunately 2 out of the 4 holsters I got have major issues with how they were made. At first I thought it was just the way the case was laying but looking closer and comparing left and right sides I see stitches on each sides are in a slightly different position, causing the front part of the case to twist to the side. This also makes putting the phone in a more challenging, and the holster doesn't stay straight with the phone in it.

Other than the fatal flaw, some of the things it does well...

*Holds my phone with case. My phone is a bit taller than the default height for the case however the strap lengthens and will fit taller phones (with case my phone has exterior dimensions of 3 1/4" by 6 1/4" by 11/16")

*Has two "compartments" so I can carry something else with it (I don't think it will fit two phones the size of mine), and I can choose which to put my phone in (the outer one seems a bit slimmer than the inner.

*The female snap buckle is attached to the case so snapping in the closure strap is fairly easy one handed

*The lining on the inside means the phone is not exposed to the back side of fastener hardware.

Again, other than the major issues I had there are a couple ways it could be better...

*I'm not a fan of the open corners or the non-zippered top, because I feel that over time the phone and inside of the case may be exposed to dust and dirt which may scratch cheap phone screens. This shouldn't be a problem on better phones with better glass.

*Inside has a nylon webbing edging that catches on my phone case when my phone screen is facing out. This would be a big annoyance if I wanted to carry my phone that way.
text_fidelity_b: East West U.S.A RTC530 Tactical Molle Attachment Smartphone Phone Holster

ASSAULTFITNESS Assault AirBike Classic, Black This is a great bike for working out. I have bad knees and so am limited in the types of exercise I can safely do. Swimming is OK once per week, but the chlorine gets to me and I don't like doing it more than that. Rowing is OK but it doesn't give me much of a lower body workout. The fancy electronic stationary bikes at the gym are fine for legs, but it is a waste of time for the upper body. Elliptical machines give a nice full body workout, but my knees won't tolerate much of that. Resistance training is also good but only once or twice per week. Pilates, Yoga and stretching are great exercises and have their place but they don't fill the need for cardio. Walking, Running, and Stair steppers are absolutely out of the question for me. So, my personal favorite form of exercise is the Dual-Action Stationary Bike for a well rounded workout that gets my heart pumping, uses all of my limbs, and puts absolutely no pressure on my knees.

For 30 years, I have enjoyed an old time Schwinn Airdyne Comp which served me well. It has preserved my health by keeping my handicap from making me hopelessly sedentary. But for the past year or so I could see the end of the line coming when my old faithful Schwinn started making unusual noises and shuddering in a strange way. Much to my surprise, I couldn't find anyone who could work on it. No one could get parts for it, no one even knew how it was put together. Even Schwinn no longer makes these and they do not support repairs of a bike that they no longer produce. I kept my Airdyne going for as long as possible, but the day finally arrived when I knew that I had done my last ride on "old Faithful". I was forced to look for a new bike.

Imagine my dismay when I set out to find a new bike and there was NOTHING that even remotely measured up to my beloved Airdyne Comp! Everything was flimsy. Everything was plastic. I even tried out one of the new-fangled Airdynes in the store and it actually collapsed with me in the saddle! Yikes! To tell the truth, I was scared that I might not find a worthy successor to the bike I had come to know and love. Then, I was researching bikes online and reading as many reviews as I could find, when one reviewer mentioned that he had returned his bike for a refund and spent the necessary bucks for and Assault Air Bike. I immediately googled that term and was delighted to find a bike that looks like the younger, cooler, and more hip granddaughter of my old, worn out Schwinn! I ordered it immediately!

It came today and I am in love! If possible, it is even better than the old Airdyne that served me so well. It was really, REALLY fast and easy to assemble because of the clearly presented video that is included in the ad on this page. Within 30 minutes, my new bike was up and running and I had my first workout. The ONLY negative is that the seat of the Assault Air Bike is atrociously painful! I am not sure why such seats are made, but by the time I finished my hour ride, I was weeping in pain. For awhile, I was regretfully considering that I might have to send the new bike to Amazon for a refund. Then, as I looked longingly at my old Airdyne Comp and dreamed about former days of riding in the comfort of the wide, cushy Schwinn seat, it dawned on me that I could probably ditch that nasty instrument of torture that came with the Assault, and replace it with my old fave, the Schwinn Airdyne Seat! Yay! Within 10 minutes, my new bike was just as comfy as the old, and I was so inspired that I indulged in a second, oh-so-comfy spin!

Some of the great features of the Assault that make it a step beyond the old Airdyne is the way the seat adjusts not only to height, but also to length. This gives a great custom fit to my body. I also learned very quickly that the onboard computer is much more complete than my old Comp and gives me great choices for incorporating HIIT training, which is just the perfect compliment to my new-found Paleo lifestyle. The new Assault computer is a little bit different in the way it counts calories, but that is not a problem for me, since I don't measure calories burned, but only time, distance, and heart rate. A few things are different that I wish they had kept but those things are minor. All in all, it is a worthy successor to my old Airdyne.

So. I purchased my Schwinn when I was 30 years old, and now I am 60. If the Assault gives me the same amount of years that I got from the Airdyne, I will be 90 by the time I need to buy yet another bike. Do you guys think the Assault will still be around by then, or should I just go ahead and purchase a back-up Assault Bike just in case? ;-)
text_fidelity_b: ASSAULTFITNESS Assault AirBike Classic, Black

text_fidelity_a:
Naneu Pro Bravo Medium Military Ops Backpack -Olive Green I did quite a bit of research before purchasing this bag for a 6 week trip through Asia. The first day I really used this bag was during a 12-hour layover in London, where I walked around the city much of the day.

I carried a Canon 40D with two relatively lightweight lenses, spare batteries, filters, and a small notebook. At the end of the day, while waiting at Heathrow for the next flight, I was shocked to notice that the bag was already beginning to fall apart! The outer fabric covering the shoulder straps had already begun to tear. So had the fabric above the zipper on the top pocket. The tear was large enough for someone to stick a hand into the pocket. I inspected the bag closely to see if something had caused these tears, but I concluded that the bag was just a piece of junk. It had begun to unravel itself under the weight of a bag that was not even half-filled!

Not having any emergency repair items on hand, the unraveling continued to get worse over the next day. Finally, I had the bag stitched up in Kerala, India, thinking that would be it. Nope! Bye the next day, the bag had unraveled in other spots as well. I had it stitched up again in Mysore, and then again in Bangalore. Thankfully, these minor fixes cost very little in India. By the time I was almost done with Bangkok, I had bought a small roll of duct tape to keep my items from falling out of the bag. I had also had countless thoughts about the negative review I would write on Amazon when I'd returned home.

I considered writing about the design and functionality of the bag, but there's really no point in doing so.

This bag is a worthless piece of junk. It's amazing that they get away with charging almost $80 for this. Naneu Pro should be ashamed for manufacturing such an inferior product, while marketing itself to be an innovative company that produces high quality goods. I'm truly shocked that Amazon and B&H Photo carry this bag. A $10 bag from the local discount store would have been more durable. What a total ripoff!
text_fidelity_b: Naneu Pro Bravo Medium Military Ops Backpack -Olive Green

Franklin Sports Kids Horseshoes Set - Soft Indoor + Outdoor Horseshoes Game Set for Kids - (4) Plastic Horseshoes, (2) Ground Stakes + (2) Plastic Indoor Stakes Included - Perfect Game for Kids This set comes with 2 blue rubber horseshoes, 2 green rubber horseshoes, 2 plastic ground stakes which can be pressed into soft soil (do not use a hammer!) and 2 free standing targets made up of a 1' wide rubber circle base, a weighted plastic stake, and a stake support base. The horseshoes are large (6.5" x 7.5")--much larger than a real horseshoe. You hold them by the top of the U and toss them at the stake. The instructions say that the stakes should be set up 10-15 feet from each other, with one team throwing from one side and the other team throwing from the other side. They suggest 4 people playing, but it works for 1-4 players. You score points if the horseshoe lands with the post inside the U (3 points) or the horseshoe touching the post (2 points) or a certain distance from the stake (1 point).

I initially used the 14" ground stakes pushed halfway into soft soil, and the stakes held well against horseshoes hitting them. The 6" free-standing stake is shorter, so a throw that might catch the ground stake and make a score might fly over the free-standing stake. I was surprised, but the free-standing stakes also took hits without falling over--probably because they're weighted and the wide circle base pulls them back down when hit. Anyway, the kids enjoyed this, though we started off much closer than 10' until they got a feel for the game. The free-standing stakes were easy to put together and take apart for storage. They do need to have dirt and grass brushed off before storage.
text_fidelity_b: Franklin Sports Kids Horseshoes Set - Soft Indoor + Outdoor Horseshoes Game Set for Kids - (4) Plastic Horseshoes, (2) Ground Stakes + (2) Plastic Indoor Stakes Included - Perfect Game for Kids

text_fidelity_a:
Hutchinson Fusion 3 Tubeless Road Tire I purchased Campy Shamal 2-way rims a couple years back. I then purchased everything needed to mount and maintain tubeless tires including Fusion 3s. I ride a '12 Specialized S-Works Roubaix and mostly do fast training rides about 3 to 4 days a week with longer rides beyond 60 miles fairly regularly. I weigh out at roughly 185 pounds.

Tubeless and ceramic bearings are somewhat in the same category these days in terms of bikers wondering if this equipment truly makes a difference. Well, I've ridden ceramic bearings in my crank and in my wheels...and YES...it makes a difference...now...I've ridden on tubeless for two riding seasons...and YES...they make a difference. Tubeless is the future...as it is in nearly every vehicle that has wheels from a riding mower to a motorcycle to a car...and mountain bikes. Why it has taken so long with road biking is understandable...change is hard...and manufacturers will go where the money is.

First, let me make this clear...putting the Fusion 3 tires on was a chore...and I mean...a CHORE. It will test your patience. Do NOT succumb to using levers as it will ruin the bead. Google tubeless tire installation for help but even then it will baffle you as to how you're going to get that tire over the rim...but...you will...and the benefits will be worth it.

Second, it takes a few rides to get the tires truly seated. Use an air compressed pump if you've got it...but...I had a "Joe Blow" floor pump that worked fine. I didn't install the sealant until after the second short ride and pump up. You will most likely lose quite a bit of air at first but as the tire seals over time...the air pressure stabilized. I do pump up my tires before every ride but it isn't out of the norm of my former clincher tires.

Third, I've ridden my fusion 3s at 90psi on the front tire and 100psi on the back. The ride is fast & super smooth. A lot of riders think super high psi is better but that is, (arguably for some), not true because at a high psi your tire is actually bumping up and down off the road which drains energy transfer over time. The benefit of running tubeless at lower psi is that the tire remains in more constant contact with the road which...over time...equals better energy transfer...and hence...speed, comfort, and endurance. Also, there is some evidence that without a tube you eliminate friction...I'm honestly not sure about that claim...even so, I can say from experience that I'm not going back to tubed tires...tubeless tires run as advertised.

Fourth, durability...I run typical roads here in Maryland over countless miles...up and down hills...less maintained side roads...and these Fusion 3s can go yet another season. The wear is normal with no unusual issues. I've NOT had one flat tire. I've NOT added more sealant since the first install...which I should've done...but...it hasn't made a difference.

Fifth, the only reservation I have is getting a flat tire but I guess it's a good thing that I'm not as use to dealing with flats like I had for my tubed tires. I have to say it has been a pleasure to not have had one flat for two seasons.

I'd like to try the ATOM version of this tire...and I think I'll get it just for comparison purposes. Not looking forward to the install and my expectation is that they will not fit my riding style, endurance expectations, and my higher weight...even so, I'm a believer in trying anything once...so...we'll see.

All in all...educate yourself but don't be afraid to go tubeless. It is change that we all seem to avoid but I'll never go back now that I've tried it out...and as the biking money goes...tubeless quality and selection will as well. ENJOY!
text_fidelity_b: Hutchinson Fusion 3 Tubeless Road Tire

text_fidelity_a:
Coleman Montana Camping Tent, 6/8 Person Family Tent with Included Rainfly, Carry Bag, and Spacious Interior, Fits Multiple Queen Airbeds and Sets Up in 15 Minutes As an adult who has just recently returned to the world of camping (I am a leader in my son's cub scout pack), I looked at LOTS of tent options before choosing the Coleman Montana 8 person tent. I checked out reviews on Amazon and CampMor, and talked to as many camping enthusiast friends as I could. My first year in scouting, I borrowed a Eureka 2-person tent from our local boy scout troop, which came up to (maybe) my waist, and just barely fit my full-sized air mattress. After struggling to change clothing while lying down (I could barely kneel, let alone stand), and suffering through a fairly sleepless/stuffy night in the Eureka tent, I decided that the following features were necessary for comfortable camping:

1. The ability to stand up fully. This meant that any tent I chose had to have a center height of at least 72", preferably more (my husband is 6 feet tall, and if I ever want him to join us camping, the tent needs to work for him too. The Montana 8 has a center height of 84" (7 feet).

2. Room for gear and at least two full/queen sized air mattresses. Although the Montana 8 states that there's room for 8 people, the diagram shows these 8 people sleeping in mummy bags very close together. From a comfort perspective, this tent will hold 4-5 people (and their gear) at a maximum, without feeling overly crowded. For the three of us, this fits the bill nicely.

3. Intuitive and easy to set up and take down. While I like camping, I am not an avid camper. Finding a tent that can be set up (and taken down) with only help from a 9 year old was key, and this fits the bill nicely.

4. Good cross-ventilation. After sleeping in a stuffy tent once, I didn't want to repeat the experience. Three windows (the two side windows and the door window) can be rolled down to allow for good air flow and ventilation. We rolled the windows down 1/3 of the way, which provided a very comfortable cross-breeze while sleeping.

5. Waterproof with a bathtub floor. Many of the reviewers stated that they had no problems with leaks along the seams without using any waterproofing sealant. After talking with others and reading some recommendations, I used the Kiwi Camp Dry Heavy Duty Water Repellent to spray the seams prior to our first use, as added protection. We had some light rain during the evening, and much heavier rain the next morning, and the inside of the tent stayed bone dry.

6. Quality. I wanted a tent that would stand up to occasional car camping trips, without having to be replaced on a regular basis. Coleman is a recognized brand, and after talking with folks who own Coleman tents and reading the reviews, I was convinced that this tent would be a good one for our family. So far, I'm pleased!

6. Price. Given that we don't do a lot of camping, I didn't want to spend hundreds on a tent. I purchased the Montana 8 in Blue (not the Elite) from Amazon in mid-May 2015, and paid $136.48; a surprisingly low price for this particular tent model/size.

Some nice features that this tent offers (that weren't on my list of must-haves):

1. A port for electrical/extension cords. While this tent does not have electricity, it does include a port near the door that allows campers to run an extension cord into the tent (for use with lanterns, fans, etc.)

2. A covered entry area. I looked at tents that had screened in areas, but opted for this one instead, choosing to have the extra room inside the tent rather than in a screened area. I had two camp chairs outside - in the evening, when it started to rain, I placed the camp chairs under the front rain fly "awning", on either side of the door. Despite the rain, the chairs stayed mostly dry, with only a few drops of water on them.

3. A "D door". This door has a pole that threads around the D curve, and another one at the hinge axis, which means that the door can function as a real door in terms of opening/closing, rather than a door that must be zipped open and closed. While there are Velcro closures around the D curve, we found that to keep insects from getting in we still had to zip it shut. However, we liked the easy entry!

All in all, my family and I are very pleased with our new tent, and look forward to many years of use!
text_fidelity_b: Coleman Montana Camping Tent, 6/8 Person Family Tent with Included Rainfly, Carry Bag, and Spacious Interior, Fits Multiple Queen Airbeds and Sets Up in 15 Minutes
